'''Arthur Bienenstock''' (born 1935) is a [[professor emeritus]] of Photon Science at [[Stanford University]]. He is also a member of the [[National Science Board]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.nsf.gov/nsb/members/ |title = National Science Board Members}}</ref>

He received his [[B.S.]] in 1955 and [[M.S.]] in 1957 from the [[Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn]], and a [[Ph.D.]] in 1962 from [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.nsf.gov/mobile/staff/staff_bio.jsp?lan=abienens&org=NSF&from_org= |title = &#124; NSF - National Science Foundation}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://web.stanford.edu/dept/app-physics/cgi-bin/person/bienenstock-arthur/ | title=Stanford University Department of Applied Physics » Arthur Bienenstock}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2005/november16/bienwmmw-111605.html | title=Road to prosperous life brings Arthur Bienenstock full circle| date=2005-11-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2015/april/bienenstock_endowed-chair-040715.html | title=Arthur Bienenstock honored with first endowed professorship to link SLAC and Stanford| newspaper=Stanford University| date=2015-04-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.ccst.us/ccstinfo/board/bios/bienenstock.php | title=Board of Directors}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?bienenstocka |title=Arthur Bienenstock &#124; Array of Contemporary American Physicists |access-date=2015-06-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618124208/http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?bienenstocka |archive-date=2015-06-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://clinton3.nara.gov/WH/EOP/OSTP/Science/html/bienenstockbio.html |title=Biography of Arthur Bienenstock |access-date=2015-06-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010726220633/http://clinton3.nara.gov/WH/EOP/OSTP/Science/html/bienenstockbio.html |archive-date=2001-07-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aiccu.edu/feed-items/arthur-bienenstock-honored-with-first-endowed-professorship-to-link-slac-and-stanford/ |title=Arthur Bienenstock honored with first endowed professorship to link SLAC and Stanford - AICCUAICCU |access-date=2015-06-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618113756/http://www.aiccu.edu/feed-items/arthur-bienenstock-honored-with-first-endowed-professorship-to-link-slac-and-stanford/ |archive-date=2015-06-18 }}</ref> He was the former director of the [[Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource]] from 1978 to 1998.

He was vice provost and dean of research at Stanford University from 2003 until 2006.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/arthur-bienenstock | title=Arthur Bienenstock's Profile &#124; Stanford Profiles}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2006/july12/newdean-071206.html|title=Ann Arvin to succeed Arthur Bienenstock as vice provost and dean of research| date=2006-07-12|work=Stanford Report|access-date=2016-10-11}}</ref>

He is a former president of the [[American Physical Society]], serving in that role in 2008,<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.aps.org/publications/capitolhillquarterly/200802/bienenstock.cfm | title=Bienenstock Elected American Physical Society President}}</ref> and was a recipient of the 2018 [[AAAS Philip Hauge Abelson Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.aaas.org/page/philip-hauge-abelson-prize-recipients | title=Philip Hauge Abelson Prize Recipients}}</ref>
